route.title: Words of Amos: Provenance and Time
route.marker: The nominal 'Words of Amos' heading supplies prophet, audience, reigns, and earthquake timing; the speech verb in 1:2 opens the first oracle.
route.rationale: Amos 1:1 completes the book's provenance-and-time superscription before 1:2 changes from narrator's heading to a voiced Zion-roar saying.
route.rejected: Keeping 1:1-2 as one retrieval unit preserves the overture but hides the formal handoff from superscription to oracle; isolating 1:1 without its overture parent would overstate autonomy.
route.basis: A complete third-person title formula ends with the earthquake locator, while the following verse begins direct prophetic speech and a new poetic image.
route.counter: The heading grammatically anticipates what Amos saw and therefore remains tightly joined to the saying it introduces.
route.guard: Hydrate the 1:1-2 overture so reign and earthquake notices remain provenance evidence rather than authorship or date rulings.

route.title: Yahweh Roars from Zion
route.marker: The speech verb opens a compact saying whose roar, voice, mourning pastures, and withered Carmel complete within one verse before the Damascus formula.
route.rationale: Amos 1:2 is a self-contained programmatic oracle: divine sound from Zion produces land-wide withering, then 1:3 restarts with a named-nation messenger formula.
route.rejected: Merging 1:2 with Damascus would treat the programmatic landscape image as Damascus's charge; merging backward with 1:1 would erase the narrator-to-oracle seam.
route.basis: Parallel roar and voice clauses yield paired environmental effects and finish before the repeated 'for three, even four' cycle begins.
route.counter: Its extreme brevity and dependence on the heading make mandatory overture hydration prudent.
route.guard: The Zion and Carmel geography must not be converted into a modern territorial or fulfillment claim.

route.title: Damascus: Threshing Gilead
route.marker: A messenger formula, three-four refrain, Damascus charge, fire verdict, broken bar, and exile closure run through 1:5; Gaza receives a fresh formula at 1:6.
route.rationale: The Damascus oracle carries one named addressee from its threshing accusation through palace fire, gate defeat, and Aram's exile, closing before the cycle restarts for Gaza.
route.rejected: A single 1:3-2:16 chunk preserves the rhetorical trap but conceals each oracle's complete charge-verdict shape; ending at 1:4 would strand the gate and exile climax.
route.basis: Repeated cycle syntax gives Damascus its own opening, offense, irreversible decision, and terminal deportation formula.
route.counter: The unit gains its full rhetorical force only as the first member of the larger nations-to-Israel sequence.
route.guard: Keep the cycle parent available and do not map ancient Damascus or Gilead language directly onto present peoples or policy.

route.title: Gaza: Communities Handed to Edom
route.marker: The Gaza addressee and numerical refrain open at 1:6; captivity charge, fire, rulers of Ashdod and Ashkelon, Ekron, and Philistine-remnant close form one oracle.
route.rationale: Gaza's mass-captivity accusation proceeds through a fire verdict into a four-city dismantling, and the remnant conclusion completes the Philistine oracle before Tyre is addressed.
route.rejected: Splitting after 1:7 would detach the city-roll consequence from Gaza's offense, while combining adjacent nations would suppress the renewed messenger formula at 1:9.
route.basis: One accusation of handing over a whole community governs the named coastal-city consequences and their final remnant sentence.
route.counter: Gaza functions as a representative heading for a wider Philistine field, so the parent cycle is essential context.
route.guard: The captivity language is literary-judicial evidence only and cannot authorize present ethnic or geopolitical identification.

route.title: Tyre: Covenant of Brotherhood Forgotten
route.marker: Tyre receives a new messenger formula and charge at 1:9; the matching fire-on-the-wall verdict closes at 1:10 before Edom begins.
route.rationale: The Tyre oracle pairs delivery of a whole community and forgetting a brotherhood covenant with a concise wall-and-palace fire judgment.
route.rejected: Merging Tyre with Gaza because their trafficking charges overlap would ignore the reset in addressee and Tyre's distinct covenant accusation.
route.basis: The numerical refrain, named city, two-part charge, and fire closure reproduce the cycle's bounded oracle grammar.
route.counter: Shared delivery-to-Edom vocabulary links Tyre backward to Gaza and warrants cycle hydration.
route.guard: The brotherhood-covenant phrase must remain an unresolved historical-literary referent, not a decided treaty or modern alliance.

route.title: Edom: Pursuit without Compassion
route.marker: Edom's formula opens with brother-pursuit, suppressed compassion, anger, and enduring wrath; fire on Teman and Bozrah closes before Ammon.
route.rationale: Four coordinated descriptions of Edom's hostility form the charge, answered by a two-city fire verdict that completes the oracle.
route.rejected: Separating the anger clauses would fragment one accumulating accusation; merging with Ammon would erase a fresh national addressee and offense.
route.basis: Kinship, pursuit, compassion, anger, and wrath create a single escalating indictment within the recurring formula-and-fire frame.
route.counter: The brother language participates in the wider neighboring-nations sequence and cannot be interpreted in isolation.
route.guard: Do not resolve the kinship referent, collective identity, or present application from the chunk boundary.

route.title: Ammon: Violence for Enlarged Borders
route.marker: The Ammon formula names violence against pregnant women for territorial gain, then fire, battle tumult, storm, and royal exile finish at 1:15.
route.rationale: Ammon's border-expansion offense receives a continuous war-and-exile verdict whose king-and-princes conclusion closes the oracle before Moab.
route.rejected: Ending at 1:14 would omit the political-exile resolution; absorbing 2:1-3 would join separate addressees merely because both end in ruler judgment.
route.basis: A motive-bearing accusation is answered by linked city, battle, weather, and leadership consequences under one speech frame.
route.counter: The severe imagery requires the surrounding cycle and historical-distance guard to avoid decontextualized use.
route.guard: The passage cannot determine present borders, collective guilt, or conduct toward descendants of an ancient name.

route.title: Moab: Desecration and the Silenced Judge
route.marker: Moab's formula and bone-burning charge open at 2:1; fire, tumult, ruler removal, and princes' death end with the speech formula at 2:3.
route.rationale: The desecration accusation moves without interruption into national tumult and the removal of judge and princes, yielding a complete Moab oracle.
route.rejected: Splitting charge from verdict would sever the oracle's judicial logic; combining with Judah would ignore the renewed formula and change from foreign king to Torah-related accusation.
route.basis: Named addressee, distinctive offense, fire judgment, leadership climax, and closing speech tag provide both boundaries.
route.counter: Its position at the chapter seam is not authority; the macro-cycle rather than numbering supplies context.
route.guard: The treatment of remains is an ancient accusation within the oracle and does not by itself define a universal legal rule.

route.title: Judah: Instruction Rejected
route.marker: Judah's renewed formula names rejection of instruction, unkept statutes, and misleading inherited falsehoods; fire on Jerusalem closes at 2:5.
route.rationale: The Judah oracle is a compact charge-and-fire verdict marked off from Moab and from the much longer Israel climax by fresh messenger formulas.
route.rejected: Merging Judah into Israel because both are covenant-facing would conceal the cycle's deliberate addressee restart at 2:6.
route.basis: Three linked clauses of instruction failure culminate in the standard palace-consuming judgment formula.
route.counter: The inherited-error wording is translation-sensitive and should not be expanded into a ruling about named traditions.
route.guard: Instruction and inherited-falsehood vocabulary remains textual evidence only; the chunk cannot adjudicate theology or living communities.

route.title: Israel: Indictment, Grace Recital, and No Escape
route.marker: Israel's formula opens a multi-charge indictment; the first-person Amorite/exodus/prophet recital grounds 2:13's verdict, and seven failed escape clauses close at 2:16.
route.rationale: The Israel climax deliberately expands the cycle from social and cultic charges through remembered divine benefaction to an inescapable judgment catalogue.
route.rejected: Splitting at 2:9 or 2:13 would isolate the grace recital or disputed pressure image from the accusations and no-escape answer they support.
route.basis: Repeated first-person acts answer Israel's conduct, and the final speed-strength-weapon-rider sequence resolves the whole accusation with exhaustive loss of escape.
route.counter: The shifts at 2:9 and 2:13 are useful internal movements, and the verb in 2:13 remains a translation hot zone.
route.guard: Hydrate the full 1:3-2:16 trap; do not use the Amorite, exodus, Nazirite, or crushing/pressing language to settle history, identity, or translation.

route.title: Hear This Word: Election, Consequence, and Prophetic Compulsion
route.marker: 'Hear this word' summons the whole exodus family; known-family accountability leads into linked rhetorical questions and the lion/prophet compulsion close at 3:8.
route.rationale: Address, relationship-based charge, cause-and-effect interrogatives, divine disclosure, and compelled proclamation form one lawsuit movement before a new foreign-witness imperative.
route.rejected: Ending at 3:2 would detach accountability from the rhetorical proof of unavoidable consequence; extending through 3:15 would absorb a fresh audience summons and renewed testimony.
route.basis: The chain repeatedly asks whether effects occur without causes, reaches Yahweh's roar and revealed counsel, and closes when fear and prophecy become unavoidable responses.
route.counter: Several compact sayings could circulate independently, but their question-chain ordering supplies cumulative logic.
route.guard: The 'known' relationship is part of the literary accusation and cannot alone settle election theology or collective status.

route.title: Foreign Witnesses over Samaria and a Torn Remnant
route.marker: A plural proclamation summons Ashdod and Egypt to Samaria; disorder and stored violence lead to an adversary verdict and shepherd-rescue simile ending at 3:12.
route.rationale: The foreign-witness scene moves from public observation to incapacity for right action, accumulated plunder, encircling adversary, and an ironic fragmentary-remnant image.
route.rejected: Keeping 3:9-15 whole preserves the lawsuit's later consequences but misses the renewed 'Hear and testify' command at 3:13; splitting before 3:12 strands the simile that qualifies the remnant.
route.basis: Summoned observers see the offense, a therefore verdict answers it, and the shepherd image closes that specific Samaria judgment before testimony restarts.
route.counter: The rescue simile contains difficult place/furniture wording and anticipates the broader house judgments in 3:13-15.
route.guard: Do not force a single translation for 3:12 or treat Ashdod/Egypt as authorities; they are actors inside the rhetoric.

route.title: Testify: Bethel Altars and Houses Fall
route.marker: A renewed plural 'Hear and testify' opens at 3:13; altar horns, winter and summer houses, ivory houses, and great houses fall through 3:15.
route.rationale: The second witness command introduces a distinct testimony whose Bethel-cult judgment expands into the collapse of elite seasonal and ivory houses.
route.rejected: Keeping 3:9-15 whole preserves the wider witness lawsuit but obscures the fresh command at 3:13; isolating 3:13 alone would leave the commanded testimony without its content.
route.basis: Renewed imperatives and a divine title lead into coordinated first-person punishments that close with the speech formula.
route.counter: Bethel and house judgments continue the Samaria indictment and require the 3:9-15 parent for rhetorical continuity.
route.guard: The altar and house images are judgment rhetoric, not authorization to target worship sites or wealth holders.

route.title: Cows of Bashan: Oath and Exile
route.marker: A feminized Bashan-cattle address names oppression and indulgent command; a holiness oath governs hook-removal and breach-exit imagery through 4:3.
route.rationale: The satirical vocative, social accusation, divine oath, and continuous exile tableau form one pointed oracle before the ironic Bethel summons.
route.rejected: Ending at 4:1 would detach accusation from oath and consequence; joining 4:4-5 would merge satire and exile with a new ironic pilgrimage speech.
route.basis: One addressed group remains the object of accusation and second-person removal verbs until the destination wording closes the scene.
route.counter: The final place/object term in 4:3 is difficult and should remain untranslated beyond the selected witness wording.
route.guard: Satire and gendered imagery cannot authorize contempt toward women, elites, or any modern group; the 4:3 translation remains open.

route.title: Come to Bethel and Multiply Transgression
route.marker: Parallel imperatives to come, transgress, bring, offer, and proclaim expose worship practice; 'for this pleases you' closes the irony before the failed-return recital.
route.rationale: Amos 4:4-5 is a compact ironic summons whose pilgrimage commands accumulate into a final explanation of the hearers' preference.
route.rejected: Merging with 4:6-11 would blur the turn from sarcastic cult description to first-person historical chastisement; splitting the parallel imperatives would destroy the irony.
route.basis: Bethel and Gilgal locations, repeated cult actions, and the closing audience appraisal create a complete satirical speech act.
route.counter: The worship critique anticipates the failed-return accusation and must not be treated as a literal ritual instruction.
route.guard: Mark the summons explicitly as irony; it is not a command to transgress or a comprehensive ruling on sacrifice.

route.title: Yet You Did Not Return: Fivefold Litany
route.marker: Five first-person calamity recollections each move toward the refrain 'yet you have not returned to me'; the fifth refrain closes at 4:11 before 'Therefore' draws consequence.
route.rationale: Famine, withheld rain, blight, pestilence, and overthrow form a deliberately patterned retrospective litany unified by the repeated failed-return response.
route.rejected: Keeping 4:6-13 as one child preserves consequence and hymn but hides the completed fivefold refrain architecture; subdividing each calamity would atomize its cumulative force.
route.basis: The identical refrain supplies five strophic closures, and its last occurrence completes the series before the discourse shifts from recollection to encounter.
route.counter: The therefore at 4:12 explicitly derives from all five strophes, so 4:12-13 needs mandatory predecessor and parent hydration.
route.guard: Do not infer a universal cause of famine, drought, disease, war, or disaster from this literary accusation.

route.title: Prepare to Meet Your God
route.marker: 'Therefore' converts the failed-return recital into a direct encounter summons; 4:13 identifies the actor through a creator-and-revealer hymn ending 'Yahweh, God of Armies, is his name.'
route.rationale: The consequence summons and its name hymn form a brief verdict-and-grounding unit, but its causal opening requires the failed-return sibling to travel with it.
route.rejected: A single 4:6-13 child better displays cumulative causality, yet the completed refrain at 4:11 and new therefore-summons justify a child seam; isolating 4:13 would detach the hymn from its host warning.
route.basis: A marked logical connector introduces second-person consequence, and the following participial hymn names and characterizes the one to be encountered.
route.counter: Both literary and canonical reviewers prefer 4:6-13 as the primary movement because 4:12 answers the refrain sequence rather than beginning independently.
route.guard: Mandatory hydration with 4:6-11; the hymn cannot be extracted as a free cosmological proof or the encounter as a timeless threat.

route.title: Fallen Virgin Israel: Funeral Lament
route.marker: 'Hear this word which I take up for a lamentation' opens a qinah-like fallen-and-unraised lament; a quantified thousand-to-hundred and hundred-to-ten verdict closes at 5:3.
route.rationale: The formal lament heading, fallen-maiden dirge, and numerical remnant saying constitute a complete funeral lament before a fresh 'Seek me and live' speech.
route.rejected: Keeping 5:1-17 whole preserves lament and response but conceals the messenger formula and imperative reset at 5:4; stopping at 5:2 would omit the interpreting decimation verdict.
route.basis: Genre is announced, the central figure is mourned, and the following verse applies the lament in parallel military-remnant ratios.
route.counter: The exhortation and public wailing that follow are the lament's rhetorical response and consequence, so the larger parent remains necessary.
route.guard: The virgin metaphor and remnant ratios must not be applied as a prediction for a modern population.

route.title: Seek Me and Live; Establish Justice
route.marker: A fresh divine saying commands seeking and living, rejects shrine-seeking, inserts a creator-name hymn, indicts justice-haters, and reaches 'Hate evil...establish justice' plus a conditional remnant appeal at 5:15.
route.rationale: The seek-live command is developed through cult warning, hymn, social indictment, prudent silence, and a renewed good-and-justice appeal whose conditional remnant clause completes the exhortation.
route.rejected: Dividing around 5:8-9 would detach the name hymn from its exhortation and accusation; merging 5:16-17 would absorb the announced consequence that begins with a fresh therefore.
route.basis: Seek/live vocabulary frames the opening and 5:14, while gate justice and good-versus-evil language carry the unit toward its conditional close.
route.counter: The hymn and accusation produce several internal movements, and 'perhaps' prevents the close from being treated as a guaranteed mechanism.
route.guard: Do not turn seeking, justice, remnant, or divine-presence statements into a formula that resolves salvation, social policy, or guaranteed outcomes.

route.title: Wailing in Every Street
route.marker: 'Therefore' and a divine title announce wailing across squares, streets, farms, and vineyards; Yahweh's passing through closes at 5:17.
route.rationale: The public mourning verdict is a complete consequence oracle that answers the prior appeal and ends with the speech formula before a new woe address.
route.rejected: Merging backward into 5:4-15 would obscure the exhortation-to-consequence turn; merging forward into 5:18 would cross the formal 'Woe' reset.
route.basis: An announced result expands spatially from city to field, then divine passage and the closing formula terminate the scene.
route.counter: Because 'therefore' depends on 5:4-15, the parent 5:1-17 should accompany retrieval.
route.guard: The professional-mourner imagery is contextual judgment rhetoric, not a judgment on mourning practices or occupations.

route.title: Woe to Those Desiring the Day
route.marker: A formal woe addresses those desiring the day; rhetorical questions, an escape-into-danger simile, and repeated darkness-not-light clauses close at 5:20.
route.rationale: The woe reverses expected desire for the day through a compact chain of question, simile, and darkness inclusio before first-person cult rejection begins.
route.rejected: Combining 5:18-27 preserves the broader worship judgment but suppresses the clear shift at 5:21; splitting the simile would break its failed-escape logic.
route.basis: The opening desire is directly challenged, illustrated by successive dangers, and restated in the final darkness/light question.
route.counter: The cult-rejection speech explains why desired observance cannot secure the day, so the larger parent remains interpretively important.
route.guard: The chunk cannot set an eschatological timetable or identify any present event as the day of Yahweh.

route.title: Rejected Worship, Wilderness Question, and Exile
route.marker: First-person rejection of feasts, assemblies, offerings, and songs opens at 5:21; justice imagery leads into the 5:25 wilderness question, disputed cult names, and exile beyond Damascus at 5:27.
route.rationale: Cult rejection, demanded justice, historical interrogation, and exile form one argumentative movement, but the question at 5:25 is strong enough to leave child retrieval unresolved.
route.rejected: Splitting 5:21-24 from 5:25-27 honors the interrogative and translation pressure yet risks detaching wilderness and exile from the worship-and-justice indictment they conclude.
route.basis: The first-person speech retains one addressee and contrasts rejected ritual with justice before testing the audience's cult history and announcing exile.
route.counter: Hebrew syntax, object names, and witness-sensitive wording in 5:25-27 make a dependent child plausible and prevent confident standalone treatment.
route.guard: Neither boundary option may select a witness, translate the cult names authoritatively, settle wilderness practice, or adjudicate later reuse.
route.hold_question: Should Amos 5:25-27 become a child unit retrievable only with mandatory hydration of Amos 5:21-24, or remain an internal seam inside one Amos 5:21-27 chunk?
hold_options: Create a dependent Amos 5:25-27 child with mandatory Amos 5:21-24 parent/sibling hydration.
Keep Amos 5:25-27 internal to one Amos 5:21-27 retrieval unit.

route.title: Woe to Complacent Zion and Samaria
route.marker: A formal woe addresses secure leaders, moves through comparative cities and luxury practices, indicts unconcern for Joseph's ruin, and reverses privilege with 'first among the exiles' at 6:7.
route.rationale: The complacency woe catalogs status, ease, music, feasting, and indifference until the opening rank is reversed into first exile and revelry ends.
route.rejected: Splitting at 6:4 or 6:6 would fragment the accumulating luxury portrait; merging 6:8-14 would cross a fresh divine oath.
route.basis: One addressed elite group persists through participial descriptions, and the therefore exile sentence answers the entire list.
route.counter: Comparative city names and bed/music images are culturally dense and require neutral historical presentation.
route.guard: The passage cannot define universal rules about comfort, art, food, or wealth, nor identify modern cities with ancient names.

route.title: Oath, Collapsing House, Justice Taunt, and Invader
route.marker: A self-sworn abhorrence opens at 6:8; city surrender, death-house scene, shattered structures, justice-turned-poison questions, false military boasting, and a raised nation culminate at 6:14.
route.rationale: The divine oath governs a sequence of total surrender, compressed house disaster, absurd justice reversal, boast exposure, and border-wide invasion.
route.rejected: Creating children at 6:9, 6:12, or 6:13 would isolate difficult scenes and taunts from the oath and invasion verdict that frame them.
route.basis: First-person resolve opens and closes the oracle, while successive rhetorical tableaux demonstrate why the proud military claim fails.
route.counter: The death-house exchange and animal-plowing idiom are difficult enough to warrant internal navigation and translation cautions.
route.guard: Keep 6:9-10 inside the unit; do not universalize death custom, resolve 6:12's animal idiom, or map the raised nation onto a current state.

route.title: Locust Vision, Intercession, and Relenting
route.marker: The showing formula introduces locust formation and consumed growth; Amos's 'How will Jacob stand?' plea receives a relenting response at 7:3 before a second showing formula.
route.rationale: The locust scene contains its own vision, catastrophe, intercession, and divine response, so it is a complete child within the paired first-two-visions parent.
route.rejected: Keeping 7:1-6 as one chunk emphasizes parallelism but erases the repeated showing formula and separate relenting conclusions; splitting before 7:3 would detach response from plea.
route.basis: A four-stage vision-dialogue sequence reaches explicit closure when Yahweh relents and says the event shall not be.
route.counter: The nearly identical fire scene is its designed companion and should always be available through parent hydration.
route.guard: Do not turn prophetic intercession and relenting into a deterministic mechanism or settle divine-change theology.

route.title: Fire Vision, Intercession, and Relenting
route.marker: A new showing formula calls for judgment by fire; consumption of the great deep and land prompts a renewed Jacob plea and a second relenting response at 7:6.
route.rationale: The fire vision repeats and intensifies the vision-catastrophe-plea-response form, closing with a distinct cancellation before the measuring-object vision.
route.rejected: Merging with 7:1-3 preserves the pair but hides separate divine responses; extending into 7:7 crosses a new visual setting and non-relenting verdict.
route.basis: Recurrent framing signals deliberate parallel scenes, while changed catastrophe and its own closing speech make the second scene independently retrievable with the pair parent.
route.counter: Its meaning depends on escalation from the locust scene, so paired hydration is mandatory.
route.guard: The great-deep and land-fire imagery cannot be mapped onto a specific disaster or cosmological scheme.

route.title: The Measuring-Object Vision
route.marker: A third showing formula places Yahweh by a wall with an uncertain measuring object; question, answer, non-passing verdict, and sanctuary/house consequences close at 7:9.
route.rationale: Object-focused vision, interpretive dialogue, and the first unrelented judgment form a complete third vision before the narrative switches to Amaziah.
route.rejected: Translating the uncertain object into the form label would make lexicography boundary authority; merging 7:10-17 would blend vision speech with narrated confrontation.
route.basis: The showing formula, visual object, divine question, prophet answer, and interpreted consequences reproduce a bounded vision-report pattern.
route.counter: The object's meaning is disputed, and the sanctuary/house verdict directly provokes the Bethel narrative.
route.guard: Use only the neutral label 'measuring object'; Hebrew roots and traditional glosses are evidence, not a decided translation or theological symbol.

route.title: Amaziah and Amos at Bethel
route.marker: Amaziah's report to Jeroboam opens a named confrontation; expulsion speech, Amos's vocation counterstatement, and a direct household/land/exile oracle reach closure at 7:17.
route.rationale: Report, royal accusation, priestly command, prophetic reply, call narrative, and counter-oracle form one complete Bethel conflict scene.
route.rejected: Isolating 7:14-15 as biography would detach the vocation statement from the accusation it answers; ending before 7:17 would omit the narrative's adjudicating counter-oracle.
route.basis: Alternating named speakers sustain a single conflict whose last prophetic speech answers Amaziah point by point and closes with exile.
route.counter: The vocation lines are highly extractable and require the full dialogue to prevent office or authorship claims from being inferred.
route.guard: Never surface 7:14-15 alone; the scene does not authorize a universal ministry model, settle Amos's occupation, or target present religious officials.

route.title: Summer Fruit and the End
route.marker: The showing formula presents a basket of summer fruit; question and answer activate the qayits/qets wordplay, then temple songs become corpses and silence at 8:3.
route.rationale: The visual sign and its wordplay interpretation proceed into a compressed wailing consequence, completing the vision before a fresh 'Hear this' summons.
route.rejected: Ending at 8:2 would omit the interpreted social result; merging 8:4-10 would cross an explicit new-audience formula.
route.basis: Object, divine question, prophet answer, phonetic interpretation, non-passing verdict, and consequence yield a full vision-dialogue unit.
route.counter: The wordplay does not transfer cleanly into English and must be explained without treating etymology as authority.
route.guard: Preserve both Hebrew lexemes as evidence only; do not infer chronology from 'the end' or isolate corpse imagery.

route.title: Hear This, You Who Trample the Needy
route.marker: 'Hear this' addresses those consuming the needy; quoted market impatience and fraud lead to a Jacob-pride oath, land upheaval, darkened noon, and feast-to-funeral reversal at 8:10.
route.rationale: Commercial intent, fraudulent practice, enslavement of the poor, divine oath, cosmic disturbance, and mourning form a charge-to-verdict movement.
route.rejected: Splitting at 8:6 or 8:7 would sever accusation from the oath that answers it; keeping through 8:14 would cross the new-days formula at 8:11.
route.basis: The oath remembers every exploitative work and governs a continuous consequence sequence ending in mourning like for an only son.
route.counter: The eclipse and earthquake imagery may be metaphorical, historical, or both; the boundary cannot decide the event mechanism.
route.guard: Economic accusations require ancient-context and whole-unit hydration; they do not directly settle a modern policy system or disaster identification.

route.title: A Famine of Hearing and the Fall of Seekers
route.marker: 'Behold, the days come' opens a word-hearing famine; sea-to-sea wandering, fainting youth, rival-oath formulas, and a final irreversible fall close at 8:14.
route.rationale: The new temporal oracle develops deprivation of hearing through futile geographic seeking and culminates in the collapse of those swearing by named cult centers.
route.rejected: Keeping 8:4-14 whole retains escalation but hides the explicit temporal reset; splitting 8:11-12 from 8:13-14 would make the hearing-famine saying dangerously portable.
route.basis: Famine, thirst, wandering, fainting, oath, and falling images build one deprivation-to-collapse sequence.
route.counter: The hearing-famine phrase is highly extractable and can be backprojected into generalized revelation or canon claims.
route.guard: Mandatory hydration with 8:4-10 and retention of 8:13-14; do not turn 'hearing the words' into a ruling on canon closure, revelation access, or present communities.

route.title: Altar Vision and the Lord of Hosts
route.marker: The altar vision opens with a strike command; descent/ascent, captivity, sea, serpent, and hostile oversight exhaust escape through 9:4, while conjunctive 9:5-6 names the cosmic sovereign who enacts it.
route.rationale: The altar catastrophe and no-escape catalogue are grounded by a creator-name hymn whose final 'Yahweh is his name' closes before direct comparison with other peoples.
route.rejected: Splitting at 9:4 would make the name hymn a free fragment despite its conjunctive grounding; keeping 9:1-10 whole would conceal the direct rhetorical reset at 9:7.
route.basis: First-person pursuit verbs elaborate the vision, and the participial hymn identifies their subject and capability before the discourse changes addressee and comparison.
route.counter: The hymn has a recognizable profile and Hebrew review preserves the 9:1-4 | 9:5-6 seam as non-blocking dissent.
route.guard: Keep the hymn attached to the altar vision; do not extract it as cosmological proof or identify the vision's historical realization.

route.title: Exodus Comparison and the Sieve
route.marker: A direct rhetorical question compares Israel, Cushites, Philistines, and Arameans; sinful-kingdom destruction is qualified by a house-preservation and sieve image before confident sinners die at 9:10.
route.rationale: Comparative migrations, discriminating judgment, sieve preservation, and the quoted complacent claim form one address movement distinct from the altar vision and restoration coda.
route.rejected: Merging 9:1-10 preserves a single judgment complex but obscures the addressee and analogy reset; extending into 9:11 crosses 'In that day' and polarity reversal.
route.basis: Questions reopen the argument, cross-people exodus analogies challenge exceptionalism, and the sieve metaphor resolves destruction versus non-total annihilation.
route.counter: The people names and sieve language are vulnerable to identity claims and require both fifth-vision and coda context.
route.guard: The comparison cannot rank modern ethnic groups, erase textual distinctions, or decide a doctrine of identity or remnant.

route.title: Raised Booth, Abundance, Return, and Planting
route.marker: 'In that day' opens a polarity reversal: the fallen booth is raised, ruins rebuilt, abundance overtakes harvest, return and rebuilding follow, and planting without uprooting closes the book.
route.rationale: Amos 9:11-15 is a strongly bounded restoration coda, but its 9:12 wording and later reuse leave the degree of mandatory judgment-context hydration unresolved.
route.rejected: Merging with 9:7-10 would hide the day formula and reversal; surfacing the coda without 9:1-10 may detach restoration from the judgment sequence and overstate one witness or later reading.
route.basis: Temporal reset, restoration verbs, agricultural reversal, return, rebuilding, planting, and a final divine speech closure create an intact coda.
route.counter: The object of possession in 9:12 is witness- and translation-sensitive, and later reuse creates strong fulfillment and identity pressures not resolvable by chunking.
route.guard: Use neutral wording and later-reuse warning; no option may choose Edom versus humanity, witness priority, Acts 15's authority relation, fulfillment, or modern land politics.
route.hold_question: Should Amos 9:11-15 be surfaced standalone with neutral wording and a later-reuse warning, or only with mandatory hydration of Amos 9:1-10?
